newsitem.title: USA: U.S. High Court to decide GM liability case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. High Court to decide GM liability case.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court said Monday it would review a ruling that threw out an $11.3 million award against General Motors Corp in a product liability case over a 1990 fatal accident involving a Chevrolet Blazer.
The justices agreed to review a U.S. appeals court ruling that overturned the jury verdict to the family of Beverly Garner, a front-seat passenger in the 1985 S-10 Blazer.
She was killed when the vehicle was involved in a head-on collision on a Missouri highway and caught fire.
The lawsuit charged the engine fire had been caused by a faulty fuel pump. The jury awarded $11.3 million in damages.
But the appeals court overturned the award in June, ruling that the jury had not been properly instructed on the issue of punitive damages.
The appeals court also ruled that trial judge had been wrong to allow a former GM employee, Ronald Elwell, to testify as a witness for the plaintiffs at trial. The appeals court ordered a new trial.
Lawyers for Garner's two sons appealed to the Supreme Court over the issue of whether Elwell should be barred from testifying.
The high court will hear arguments in the case during its term that begins in October, with a decision expected early next year.
